court: High Court of Judicature at Madras

parties.respondent_defendant: Mr.Anil Nahar, defendants; M/s.Transworld Exports (P) Ltd, represented by its Director, Mr.Anil Nahar

facts_of_case: The plaintiff and the 1st defendant are sons of late D.C.Nahar. The father entered into an agreement to purchase an immovable property. The property was purchased substantially under sale deed dated 12.09.1973. The suit is for partition by way of declaring the plaintiff's one half share in the suit properties.

legal_principles.principle: A Class-I legal heir is entitled to an equal share in the estate left behind by a deceased person.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiff was entitled to an equal share in the estate left behind by the D.C.Nahar along with the 1st defendant, who is the other son.

legal_principles.principle: When a transfer is established to be fraudulent, the original owner's heirs are entitled to the transferred property.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiff was entitled to one half of the said 22500 shares, namely 11250 shares.

outcome.final_order: The court declared the plaintiff's half share in the suit schedule properties and appointed a Commissioner for division of the properties. The defendants were restrained from encumbering or alienating the suit schedule properties.
